title: Verb Conjugation & Tenses (Konjugation & Zeiten)
summary: Master German verb mechanics: regular present-tense personal endings, stem-vowel mutations, irregular auxiliaries (haben/sein/werden), modal verbs, and past participle formations.

tables.title: Regular Present Tense Endings (Präsens)
tables.description: Standard personal endings attached to the verb stem (e.g., lern-en).

tables.title: The Irregular Auxiliaries (sein, haben, werden)
tables.description: The three most essential verbs in the German language, also serving as auxiliary verbs for compound tenses.

tables.title: Stem-Vowel Changes (du & er/sie/es only)
tables.description: In strong verbs, vowel changes occur ONLY in the 2nd (du) and 3rd person singular (er/sie/es).

tables.title: Modal Verbs (Modalverben)
tables.description: Notice: 1st (ich) and 3rd person singular (er/sie/es) are identical and have NO ending.

rules.name: The Sentence Bracket (Satzklammer)
rules.explanation: When two verbal elements occur in a German main clause (e.g. Modal Verb + Infinitive, or Perfekt Auxiliary + Participle, or Separable Verb), the conjugated verb goes into Position 2, and the second verbal element goes to the very end of the clause.

examples.english: Unfortunately, I cannot come this evening.
examples.breakdown: kann (modal) at Position 2, kommen (infinitive) at the very end

examples.german: Er <verb>steht</verb> jeden Morgen um sechs Uhr <prefix>auf</prefix>.
examples.english: He gets up every morning at six o'clock.
examples.breakdown: steht (conjugated stem) at Position 2, auf (separable prefix) at the end
